Standard deviation and Euclidean distance (C backend)

Source: R/prim.R
cspread.Rd

csdev() returns the standard deviation of a numeric vector and cdistm() the straight-line (Euclidean) distance between two vectors of the same length.

Usage

csdev(x, ddof = 1L)

cdistm(a, b)

Arguments

x, a, b

Numeric (or logical) vectors; a and b of the same length.

ddof

The delta degrees of freedom, one whole number from 0: the divisor is n - ddof.

Value

A number: the standard deviation in the units of x, or the distance in the units of a and b.

Details

csdev() computes $$s = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n - \mathrm{ddof}} \sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar x)^2},$$ so ddof = 1 is the sample standard deviation of stats::sd() and ddof = 0 the population figure. cdistm() computes \(\sqrt{\sum_i (a_i - b_i)^2}\).

Missing values propagate: one NA makes the result NA. A vector with no more than ddof values has no defined spread and gives NaN. Two empty vectors are at distance 0. Text, a factor, a list or a data frame is refused, and so are a and b of different lengths; logical input counts as 0 and 1.

See also

cmom(), cmad().

Examples

csdev(c(2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9))
#> [1] 2.13809
all.equal(csdev(1:10), stats::sd(1:10))
#> [1] TRUE
csdev(1:10, ddof = 0)
#> [1] 2.872281
csdev(c(3, NA, 5))
#> [1] NA
cdistm(c(0, 0), c(3, 4))
#> [1] 5
try(cdistm(1:3, 1:2))
#> Error : cdistm: `a` and `b` must have the same length.
